notes: POC objective: validate Dedicated throughput guarantees and latency SLOs for real-time bridge-assist chat (safety-critical prompts).

Representative prompt: 'BridgeAssist: Captain sees unknown object at bearing 142, distance 0.8nm. Provide recommended maneuvers and radio comms summary (3 bullets).' — typical response target: 40-120 tokens.
Acceptance criteria (customer): p95 latency <= 120ms for <=128-token responses; sustained throughput 6k tokens/sec with <1% error rate; 48h soak with no quality regressions vs baseline.
Hardware ask from Mariner: equivalent of 8x A100-80GB preferred for headroom; procurement will accept 12x A10 as lower-cost alternative if latency SLOs demonstrably met.
Routing/fallback plan: route to L2-70B-int8 by default; if queue depth or latencies spike, fall back to Mistral-7B (cheaper) or degraded response mode (shorter summaries) to preserve SLOs.
Cost sensitivity: mid/enterprise budget but focused on predictable monthly reserved commitment — interested in 12 month reserved capacity (Dedicated) with soft burst credits.
Quality measurement: Redwood to run side-by-side evals using Mariner prompts + human eval on 200 sample cases; baseline quality metric must be within 5% of incumbent for go-live.
SLA negotiation points: uptime threshold, latency credit formula, escalation path (SE -> Solutions -> Engineering), and allowed maintenance windows (prefer off-peak UTC).
Procurement timeline: Mariner aims to finalize internal approval by 2026-04-15; legal to confirm SLA language before order commit.
Open tech question: confirmation of GPU packing layout for KV cache locality — affects cold-start latency. SE recommended colocating KV store on same rack for warm cache hits.
Test anomalies: transient 502s observed at minute 22 of previous load run when model swap occurred; action item to add graceful draining for model rollouts.
Customer quote: 'If we can hit p95 120ms consistently during heavy traffic, we can consolidate three legacy inference clusters.' — Head of Autonomy (Mariner).
